note: Questions from the CBSE Class XII Chemistry board exam 2025, Q.P. code 56/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Structural formulae are written out in words or condensed formulae. Solutions are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In case of association, the abnormal molar mass of the solute will
questions.solution: Association reduces the number of particles, so colligative properties fall and the calculated molar mass comes out higher.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The standard electrode potential for the Sn⁴⁺/Sn²⁺ couple is +0.15 V and that for the Cr³⁺/Cr couple is −0.74 V. The two couples in their standard states are connected to make a cell. The cell potential will be
questions.solution: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.15 − (−0.74) = 0.89 V.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The magnetic moment is associated with spin angular momentum and orbital angular momentum. The spin-only magnetic moment of the Cr³⁺ ion (atomic number of Cr = 24) is
questions.solution: Cr³⁺ is 3d³ with n = 3 unpaired electrons: μ = √(n(n + 2)) = √15 ≈ 3.87 B.M.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Acidified KMnO₄ oxidises sulphite to
questions.solution: 5SO₃²⁻ + 2MnO₄⁻ + 6H⁺ → 5SO₄²⁻ + 2Mn²⁺ + 3H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂]²⁺ is
questions.solution: x + 0 − 2 = +2 gives Pt in +4. The complex is a cation, so the metal name is unchanged.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their boiling points: (i) (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Br (ii) CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂Br (iii) (CH₃)₃CBr
questions.solution: Boiling point falls with branching (smaller surface area): tert-butyl < isobutyl < n-butyl bromide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Alkyl halides undergoing nucleophilic bimolecular substitution reaction involve
questions.solution: In SN2 the nucleophile attacks from the back side in a single step, inverting the configuration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which is the correct order of acid strength from the following?
questions.solution: The phenoxide ion is resonance stabilised; alkyl groups (+I) make alcohols weaker acids than water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The acid formed when propyl magnesium bromide is treated with CO₂ followed by acid hydrolysis is :
questions.solution: RMgX + CO₂ then H₃O⁺ gives RCOOH with one extra carbon: butanoic acid, C₃H₇COOH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The best reagent for converting propanamide into propanamine is
options: iodine in the presence of red phosphorus
questions.solution: LiAlH₄ reduces the amide CH₃CH₂CONH₂ to CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂, keeping all three carbons. (Hofmann bromamide would give ethanamine.)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following statements is not true about glucose?
options: On heating with HI it forms n-hexane.
It does not give Schiff's test.
questions.solution: Glucose exists in the six-membered pyranose form, not the furanose form.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: An unripe mango placed in a concentrated salt solution to prepare pickle shrivels because
options: it gains water due to osmosis
it loses water due to reverse osmosis
it gains water due to reverse osmosis
it loses water due to osmosis
questions.solution: The salt solution is hypertonic, so water moves out of the mango by osmosis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): [Cr(H₂O)₆]Cl₂ and [Fe(H₂O)₆]Cl₂ are examples of homoleptic complexes.
Reason (R): All the ligands attached to the metal are the same.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Homoleptic complexes have only one kind of ligand bonded to the metal; here all six are H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The boiling points of alkyl halides decrease in the order RI > RBr > RCl > RF.
Reason (R): The boiling points of alkyl chlorides, bromides and iodides are considerably higher than that of the hydrocarbon of comparable molecular mass.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Both are true. The order in A comes from increasing size and van der Waals forces; R compares with hydrocarbons and does not explain the order.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The boiling point of ethanol is higher than that of methoxymethane.
Reason (R): There is intramolecular hydrogen bonding in ethanol.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: A is true, but the reason is intermolecular hydrogen bonding in ethanol, so R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): All naturally occurring α-amino acids except glycine are optically active.
Reason (R): Most naturally occurring amino acids have L-configuration.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Both are true, but optical activity comes from the chiral α-carbon (glycine has two H atoms on it), not from the L-configuration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Give reasons :
(a) Cooking is faster in a pressure cooker than in an open pan.
(b) On mixing liquid X and liquid Y, the volume of the resulting solution decreases. What type of deviation from Raoult's law is shown by the resulting solution? What change in temperature would you observe after mixing liquids X and Y?
questions.solution: (a) The higher pressure inside raises the boiling point of water, so food cooks at a higher temperature. (b) A decrease in volume means stronger X–Y attractions: negative deviation. Heat is released (ΔH_mix < 0), so the temperature rises.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Define azeotrope. What type of azeotrope is formed by negative deviation from Raoult's law? Give an example.
questions.solution: An azeotrope is a liquid mixture that boils at a constant temperature and has the same composition in liquid and vapour, so it cannot be separated by fractional distillation. Negative deviation forms a maximum-boiling azeotrope, e.g. about 68% nitric acid and water (or HCl and water).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Complete and balance the following chemical equations :
(a) 2MnO₄⁻(aq) + 10I⁻(aq) + 16H⁺(aq) →
(b) Cr₂O₇²⁻(aq) + 6Fe²⁺(aq) + 14H⁺(aq) →
questions.solution: (a) 2MnO₄⁻ + 10I⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5I₂ + 8H₂O. (b) Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 6Fe²⁺ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 6Fe³⁺ + 7H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Would you expect benzaldehyde to be more reactive or less reactive in nucleophilic addition reactions than propanal? Justify your answer.
questions.solution: Less reactive. In benzaldehyde, resonance with the benzene ring reduces the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon, making it less electrophilic than in propanal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Identify A and B in each of the following reaction sequences :
(a) CH₃CH₂Cl —NaCN→ A —H₂/Ni→ B
(b) C₆H₅NH₂ —NaNO₂/HCl, 0–5 °C→ A —C₆H₅NH₂, H⁺→ B
questions.solution: (a) A = CH₃CH₂CN (propanenitrile), B = CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂ (propan-1-amine). (b) A = C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ (benzenediazonium chloride), B = p-aminoazobenzene, C₆H₅–N=N–C₆H₄–NH₂ (a yellow dye).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Write the reactions involved when D-glucose is treated with the following reagents : (a) HCN (b) Br₂ water
questions.solution: (a) The aldehyde group adds HCN to give glucose cyanohydrin: CHO–(CHOH)₄–CH₂OH + HCN → CH(OH)CN–(CHOH)₄–CH₂OH. (b) Bromine water oxidises the –CHO group to –COOH, giving gluconic acid: HOOC–(CHOH)₄–CH₂OH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A solution of glucose (molar mass 180 g mol⁻¹) in water has a boiling point of 100.20 °C. Calculate the freezing point of the same solution. The molal constants for water K_f and K_b are 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹ and 0.512 K kg mol⁻¹ respectively.
questions.solution: ΔT_b = 0.20 K = K_b m, so m = 0.20/0.512 = 0.39 mol/kg. ΔT_f = K_f m = 1.86 × 0.39 ≈ 0.73 K. Freezing point ≈ −0.73 °C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) State : (i) Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions and (ii) Faraday's first law of electrolysis.
(b) Using the E° values of X and Y given below, predict which is better for coating the surface of iron to prevent corrosion and why. E°(X²⁺/X) = −2.36 V, E°(Y²⁺/Y) = −0.14 V, E°(Fe²⁺/Fe) = −0.44 V.
questions.solution: (a)(i) The limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte is the sum of the limiting ionic conductivities of its cation and anion, each multiplied by the number of those ions. (ii) The mass of substance deposited or liberated at an electrode is proportional to the quantity of electricity passed: m = ZQ. (b) X, because its reduction potential is lower than iron's: it is oxidised in preference to iron and protects it (sacrificial protection) even if the coating is scratched.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A certain reaction is 50% complete in 20 minutes at 300 K and the same reaction is 50% complete in 5 minutes at 350 K. Calculate the activation energy if it is a first order reaction. [R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; log 4 = 0.602]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
The elements of the 3d transition series are Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn. Answer the following :
(a) Copper has an exceptionally positive E°(M²⁺/M) value. Why?
(b) Which element is a strong reducing agent in the +2 oxidation state and why?
(c) Zn²⁺ salts are colourless. Why?
questions.solution: (a) Copper's high enthalpy of atomisation and ionisation enthalpies are not balanced by its hydration enthalpy, so changing Cu(s) to Cu²⁺(aq) is unfavourable. (b) Cr²⁺: it is easily oxidised to Cr³⁺, which has the stable half-filled t₂g³ configuration. (Ti²⁺ and V²⁺ are also reducing.) (c) Zn²⁺ is 3d¹⁰ with no unpaired electrons, so no d–d transitions are possible.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Write the major monohalo product of each reaction :
(a) 1-chloro-4-ethylbenzene with Br₂ and heat
(b) 1-methylcyclohexene with HBr
(c) 4-(hydroxymethyl)phenol (HOCH₂–C₆H₄–OH) with HCl and heat
questions.solution: (a) Free-radical substitution at the benzylic carbon: 1-(1-bromoethyl)-4-chlorobenzene, Cl–C₆H₄–CH(Br)CH₃. (b) Markovnikov addition: 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane. (c) Only the alcoholic –OH is replaced (the phenolic –OH is not): 4-(chloromethyl)phenol, ClCH₂–C₆H₄–OH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: How do you convert : (a) Chlorobenzene to biphenyl (b) Propene to 1-iodopropane (c) 2-bromobutane to but-2-ene?
questions.solution: (a) Fittig reaction: 2C₆H₅Cl + 2Na (dry ether) → C₆H₅–C₆H₅ + 2NaCl. (b) Anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr with peroxide gives 1-bromopropane, then Finkelstein reaction with NaI in acetone gives 1-iodopropane. (c) Heat with alcoholic KOH (dehydrohalogenation, Saytzeff rule) to give but-2-ene as the major product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their boiling points : (CH₃)₂NH, CH₃CH₂NH₂, CH₃CH₂OH.
(b) Give a plausible explanation for each of the following : (i) Aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis. (ii) Amides are less basic than amines.
questions.solution: (a) (CH₃)₂NH < CH₃CH₂NH₂ < CH₃CH₂OH (hydrogen bonding is weaker in the secondary amine and strongest in the alcohol). (b)(i) Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion. (ii) In amides the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised onto the C=O group by resonance, so it is less available for protonation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) What is the difference between a native protein and a denatured protein?
(b) Which one of the following is a disaccharide? Glucose, Lactose, Amylose, Fructose
(c) Which vitamin is responsible for the coagulation of blood?
questions.solution: (a) A native protein has its natural 3D (secondary and tertiary) structure and is biologically active. Denaturation (by heat, pH change, etc.) destroys these structures, leaving the primary structure, and the protein loses its activity. (b) Lactose. (c) Vitamin K.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
The rate of a chemical reaction is expressed either in terms of the decrease in concentration of reactants or the increase in concentration of a product per unit time. It depends on the nature and concentration of reactants, temperature, catalyst, surface area and light. The rate law states that the rate depends on the concentration terms on which the rate actually depends, as observed experimentally. The sum of powers of the concentrations in the rate law is the order of the reaction, while the number of reacting species which must collide simultaneously in an elementary reaction is its molecularity.

(i) What is a rate determining step? (ii) Define a complex reaction.
questions.solution: (i) The slowest step in a reaction mechanism, which controls the overall rate. (ii) A reaction that takes place in more than one elementary step (a sequence of steps) is a complex reaction.

questions.text:

It depends on the nature and concentration of reactants, temperature, catalyst, surface area and light. The rate law states that the rate depends on the concentration terms on which the rate actually depends, as observed experimentally. The sum of powers of the concentrations in the rate law is the order of the reaction, while the number of reacting species which must collide simultaneously in an elementary reaction is its molecularity.

What is the effect of temperature on the rate constant of a reaction?
questions.solution: The rate constant increases with temperature; for many reactions it roughly doubles for a 10 °C rise (Arrhenius equation k = Ae^(−Ea/RT)).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
The rate of a chemical reaction is expressed either in terms of the decrease in concentration of reactants or the increase in concentration of a product per unit time. It depends on the nature and concentration of reactants, temperature, catalyst, surface area and light. The rate law states that the rate depends on the concentration terms on which the rate actually depends, as observed experimentally. The sum of powers of the concentrations in the rate law is the order of the reaction, while the number of reacting species which must collide simultaneously in an elementary reaction is its molecularity.

Why is molecularity applicable only to elementary reactions whereas order is applicable to elementary as well as complex reactions?
questions.solution: Molecularity is the number of species colliding in one step, which has meaning only for a single elementary step. Order is found experimentally from the overall rate law, so it applies to any reaction.

It depends on the nature and concentration of reactants, temperature, catalyst, surface area and light. The rate law states that the rate depends on the concentration terms on which the rate actually depends, as observed experimentally. The sum of powers of the concentrations in the rate law is the order of the reaction, while the number of reacting species which must collide simultaneously in an elementary reaction is its molecularity.

The conversion of molecule X to Y follows second order kinetics. If the concentration of X is increased 3 times, how will it affect the rate of formation of Y?
questions.solution: Rate ∝ [X]², so the rate increases 3² = 9 times.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Phenols undergo electrophilic substitution reactions readily due to the strong activating effect of the OH group attached to the benzene ring. Since the OH group increases the electron density more at the ortho and para positions, it is ortho, para-directing. The Reimer-Tiemann reaction is an example of an aldehyde group being introduced on the aromatic ring of phenol, ortho to the hydroxyl group. It is a general method for the ortho-formylation of phenols.

What happens when phenol reacts with (i) Br₂ in CS₂ (ii) conc. HNO₃?
questions.solution: (i) In a non-polar solvent at low temperature, monobromination gives a mixture of o-bromophenol and p-bromophenol (para major). (ii) Concentrated nitric acid gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Phenols undergo electrophilic substitution reactions readily due to the strong activating effect of the OH group attached to the benzene ring. Since the OH group increases the electron density more at the ortho and para positions, it is ortho, para-directing. The Reimer-Tiemann reaction is an example of an aldehyde group being introduced on the aromatic ring of phenol, ortho to the hydroxyl group. It is a general method for the ortho-formylation of phenols.

Why does phenol not undergo protonation readily?
questions.solution: The lone pairs on the oxygen are delocalised into the benzene ring by resonance, so they are less available to accept a proton.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Phenols undergo electrophilic substitution reactions readily due to the strong activating effect of the OH group attached to the benzene ring. Since the OH group increases the electron density more at the ortho and para positions, it is ortho, para-directing. The Reimer-Tiemann reaction is an example of an aldehyde group being introduced on the aromatic ring of phenol, ortho to the hydroxyl group. It is a general method for the ortho-formylation of phenols.

Which is a stronger acid, phenol or cresol? Give reason.
questions.solution: Phenol. The methyl group in cresol is electron-releasing, which destabilises the phenoxide ion and so lowers acidity.

questions.text:
Phenols undergo electrophilic substitution reactions readily due to the strong activating effect of the OH group attached to the benzene ring. Since the OH group increases the electron density more at the ortho and para positions, it is ortho, para-directing. The Reimer-Tiemann reaction is an example of an aldehyde group being introduced on the aromatic ring of phenol, ortho to the hydroxyl group. It is a general method for the ortho-formylation of phenols.

Write the IUPAC name of the product formed in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.
questions.solution: 2-Hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) Write the cell reaction and calculate the emf of the following cell at 298 K : Sn(s) | Sn²⁺ (0.004 M) || H⁺ (0.02 M) | H₂(g) (1 bar) | Pt(s). (Given : E°(Sn²⁺/Sn) = −0.14 V, E°(H⁺/H₂) = 0.00 V)
(b) Account for the following : (i) On the basis of E° values, O₂ gas should be liberated at the anode, but it is Cl₂ gas which is liberated in the electrolysis of aqueous NaCl. (ii) Conductivity of CH₃COOH decreases on dilution.
questions.solution: (a) Sn + 2H⁺ → Sn²⁺ + H₂. E°cell = 0.14 V. E = 0.14 − (0.0591/2) log([Sn²⁺]/[H⁺]²) = 0.14 − 0.02955 log(0.004/0.0004) = 0.14 − 0.02955 × 1 ≈ 0.11 V. (b)(i) Oxygen evolution has a high overpotential, so in practice Cl⁻ is oxidised more easily. (ii) Conductivity is conductance per unit volume; on dilution the number of ions per unit volume decreases, although molar conductivity increases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) Write the anode and cathode reactions and the overall cell reaction occurring in a lead storage battery during its use.
(b) Calculate the potential for a half-cell containing 0.01 M K₂Cr₂O₇(aq), 0.01 M Cr³⁺(aq) and 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ M H⁺(aq). The half-cell reaction is Cr₂O₇²⁻(aq) + 14H⁺(aq) + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺(aq) + 7H₂O(l), and E° = 1.33 V. [Given : log 10 = 1]
questions.solution: (a) Anode: Pb + SO₄²⁻ → PbSO₄ + 2e⁻. Cathode: PbO₂ + SO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺ + 2e⁻ → PbSO₄ + 2H₂O. Overall: Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄ → 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O. (b) E = 1.33 − (0.0591/6) log([Cr³⁺]²/([Cr₂O₇²⁻][H⁺]¹⁴)) = 1.33 − (0.0591/6) log(10⁻⁴/(10⁻² × 10⁻⁵⁶)) = 1.33 − (0.0591/6)(54) ≈ 1.33 − 0.53 = 0.80 V.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Answer the following :
(a) Low spin tetrahedral complexes are not known.
(b) Co²⁺ is easily oxidised to Co³⁺ in the presence of a strong ligand. [At. No. of Co = 27]
(c) What type of isomerism is shown by the complex [Co(NH₃)₆][Cr(CN)₆]?
(d) Why is a solution of [Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺ green while a solution of [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is colourless? (At. No. of Ni = 28)
(e) Write the IUPAC name of the complex [Co(NH₃)₅(CO₃)]Cl.
questions.solution: (a) The tetrahedral splitting Δt (about 4/9 Δo) is always smaller than the pairing energy, so electrons do not pair and low spin does not arise. (b) Strong ligands cause large splitting; Co³⁺ (d⁶) then gets the very stable t₂g⁶ low-spin configuration, so the large crystal field stabilisation drives the oxidation. (c) Coordination isomerism. (d) [Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺ has Ni²⁺ (d⁸) with two unpaired electrons in a weak field, allowing d–d transitions in the visible region (green). [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is square planar (dsp²) with all electrons paired and no visible d–d absorption, so it is colourless. (e) Pentaamminecarbonatocobalt(III) chloride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) What is meant by the 'chelate effect'? Give an example.
(b) Write the hybridisation and magnetic behaviour of [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻. (Atomic number : Fe = 26)
(c) If PtCl₂·2NH₃ does not react with AgNO₃, what will be its formula?
questions.solution: (a) Complexes with chelating (polydentate) ligands are more stable than similar complexes with monodentate ligands; e.g. [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ is more stable than [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺, and EDTA complexes are very stable. (b) Fe²⁺ (3d⁶) with strong-field CN⁻ pairs up all electrons: d²sp³ hybridisation, octahedral, diamagnetic. (c) No free Cl⁻ ions, so both Cl are in the coordination sphere: [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂].

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) Carry out the following conversions : (i) Ethanal to but-2-enal (ii) Propanoic acid to ethane
(b) An alkene A with molecular formula C₅H₁₀ on ozonolysis gives a mixture of two compounds B and C. Compound B gives a positive Fehling test and also reacts with iodine and NaOH solution. Compound C does not give the Fehling test but forms iodoform. Identify the compounds A, B and C.
questions.solution: (a)(i) Aldol condensation: 2CH₃CHO with dilute NaOH gives CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO, which on heating loses water to give CH₃CH=CHCHO. (ii) Convert propanoic acid to its sodium salt with NaOH, then heat with soda lime (decarboxylation): CH₃CH₂COONa + NaOH (CaO) → CH₃CH₃ + Na₂CO₃. (b) B is an aldehyde giving iodoform: ethanal, CH₃CHO. C is a methyl ketone that is not an aldehyde: propanone, CH₃COCH₃. So A = (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₃, 2-methylbut-2-ene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: An organic compound A (molecular formula C₈H₁₆O₂) was hydrolysed with dilute sulphuric acid to give a carboxylic acid B and an alcohol C. Oxidation of C with chromic acid produced B. C on dehydration gives but-1-ene. Identify A, B and C and write chemical equations for the reactions involved.
questions.solution: C gives but-1-ene, so C is butan-1-ol, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH. Its oxidation gives B = butanoic acid, CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH. A is the ester butyl butanoate, CH₃CH₂CH₂COOCH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₈H₁₆O₂). Equations: A + H₂O (H⁺) → CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH + CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH; CH₃(CH₂)₃OH + [O] (H₂CrO₄) → CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH; CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH (conc. H₂SO₄, heat) → CH₃CH₂CH=CH₂ + H₂O.
